attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition keeps the hedge 'does not seem'. It is a hedged present-tense impression, partly hyperbolic, and it gives no standard for 'enough'.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to set a binary condition. Scoring it would mean inventing a sufficiency goal and turning a hedged impression into a categorical claim.

evidence.note: A 2022 projection that high-quality language data would run out. It is about future exhaustion, not a measured insufficiency in 2023.
A company disclosure that OpenAI licensed AP's archive. It shows a developer sought licensed data, not that the public internet was insufficient.

reviews.rationale: 'Doesn't seem to be enough' is a hedged impression, and it names no task or threshold that would define 'enough'. No fair test exists without adding standards the speaker never gave. The evidence only explains the background concern.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition restores the qualifiers 'much of what it needed' and 'all your personal data'. It is a firm present-tense claim that something does not exist.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. It means a broadly effective alternative that avoids extensive use of personal data, judged as of the post date. Narrow successes are rightly excluded and no stretched threshold is imposed.

evidence.note: DreamCoder (2020) is an alternative approach, but only in narrow domains. It does not show broad effectiveness in the world.
Gato is broad, but it extends the large-scale language-modelling approach and has no data-independence finding. It neither supports nor contradicts the claim.
I-JEPA (April 2023) is an alternative confined to image learning. It does not show broad effectiveness.

reviews.rationale: No item meets the contradiction condition, because each alternative is either narrow or not data-independent. No comprehensive contemporary assessment establishes nonexistence either, which the support condition requires. Failing to find a counterexample is not enough, so the packet does not settle the claim.
